description:
Creates or opens a disposable, receive-only email inbox and reads what arrived — to sign up somewhere and get the verification code or confirmation link without using the user's real address.

WHEN TO USE: a site or service asks for an email to send a code, a magic link or a confirmation, and the user does not want to give their own; or you need to read what was sent to an inbox created earlier.

HOW IT WORKS:
- inbox: a name ("fulano") or a full address on the tool's domain. Empty: a random, hard-to-guess address is created. Any name works: there is no sign-up.
- waitSeconds (0–50, default 0): wait for a NEW message to arrive before answering. Typical flow: call once with no inbox to get an address, give it to the site, then call again with that inbox and waitSeconds 30–50 until the email shows up.
- message: the id of one message, to read it in full (text, links, attachments).
- The inbox is PUBLIC: anyone who knows the address can read it. Never use it for banking, government or any account the user wants to keep.
- Receive only (it cannot send). Messages up to 10 MB; everything is deleted after 8 days. Some sites refuse disposable domains — then the user needs a real address.

RETURNS: address; messages (newest first) with id, from, subject, preview, receivedAt and code — the verification code when one is found; with message, also text, links (url and text, confirmation links included) and attachments. link: this inbox on the web page, to show the user. timedOut is true when waitSeconds ended with no new message.

inbox.description: The inbox: a name, or name@domain on this tool's domain. Empty: a new random address.

message.description: The id of a message in this inbox, to read it in full.

waitSeconds.description: How long to wait for a new message before answering, 0 to 50 seconds. 0 (default) answers at once.
